summary.title: Scenario 3: Microservices Healthcare Application
summary.description: A microservices-based patient management system with OAuth 2.0 authentication, JWT tokens, and multiple internal services exposed via an API gateway.

threats.title: Patient Portal Session Hijacking
threats.description: An attacker intercepts or steals a patient's active session cookie from the patient portal to hijack their authenticated session and access medical records without re-authentication.
threats.mitigation: Use HTTPOnly and Secure cookie flags, implement session timeout, regenerate session tokens after login, enforce HTTPS per OWASP Top 10 A02, and use multi-factor authentication.

threats.title: JWT Token Forgery
threats.description: An attacker forges or replays a stolen JWT token to impersonate a legitimate patient and gain unauthorized access to medical records through the API gateway.
threats.mitigation: Use short JWT expiry times, implement token blacklisting, validate JWT signatures using strong algorithms (RS256), and enforce token binding to client IP.

threats.title: DDoS Attack on API Gateway
threats.description: An attacker floods the API gateway with massive amounts of requests, overwhelming the system and making patient portal, medical records, and appointment services unavailable to legitimate users.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting, use Web Application Firewall (WAF), enable auto-scaling, apply OWASP Top 10 A05 security misconfiguration controls, and use DDoS protection services.

threats.title: OAuth Token Theft
threats.description: An attacker intercepts OAuth 2.0 access tokens during transmission between the identity service and API gateway, gaining unauthorized access to patient data and internal services.
threats.mitigation: Enforce TLS 1.3 for all inter-service communication, use short-lived tokens, implement PKCE for OAuth flows, and monitor for unusual token usage patterns.

threats.title: Brute Force on Identity Service
threats.description: An attacker repeatedly sends authentication requests to the identity service to exhaust its resources, preventing legitimate patients from logging in and accessing medical records or booking appointments.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting on authentication endpoints, use account lockout policies, deploy CAPTCHA after multiple failures, and monitor login attempts per NIST 800-53 AC-7.

threats.title: Unauthorized Patient Record Access
threats.description: An attacker exploits weak authorization checks in the medical records service to access other patients' confidential health records, violating HIPAA compliance requirements.
threats.mitigation: Implement role-based access control (RBAC), enforce patient-level authorization checks, log all record access attempts, and comply with NIST 800-53 AC-3 access enforcement controls.

threats.title: Appointment Data Repudiation
threats.description: A patient or staff member denies booking or cancelling an appointment, and the system lacks sufficient audit trails to prove the action occurred, leading to scheduling disputes and potential patient harm.
threats.mitigation: Implement comprehensive audit logging for all appointment actions with timestamps and user IDs, use digital signatures per NIST 800-53 AU-9, and store logs in a tamper-proof system.

threats.title: Medical Records Data Tampering
threats.description: An attacker with database access modifies patient medical records, altering diagnoses, prescriptions, or treatment history, potentially causing life-threatening medical errors.
threats.mitigation: Implement database integrity checks, use write-ahead logging, enforce strict access controls per NIST 800-53 SI-7, encrypt data at rest, and maintain immutable audit logs of all record modifications.

threats.title: Patient Data Exposure via Notification
threats.description: Sensitive patient information such as diagnosis details or appointment reasons is included in SMS or email notifications sent through third-party providers, exposing PHI to unauthorized parties.
threats.mitigation: Minimize PHI in notifications, use generic messages without sensitive details, encrypt notification content, and ensure third-party providers are HIPAA compliant per ISO 27001 controls.

threats.title: Third-Party Provider Compromise
threats.description: A compromised third-party SMS or email provider sends fake appointment reminders to patients, and there is no way to verify the authenticity of messages sent through the provider.
threats.mitigation: Implement message signing, use DKIM and SPF records for email authentication, monitor provider activity logs, and maintain contracts requiring ISO 27001 compliance from third-party providers.
